plan/PHASE6-TEACHING.md.purpose: Researched and now implemented-locally plan for Phase 6.2 demonstration teaching: record an owner demonstration on a bot desktop, review evidence, generate/edit/test a SKILL.md candidate and publish it natively. Remains the acceptance contract.

responsibilities.text: Status header: recorded Oct 27 2026; implementation authorized and built locally; real owner acceptance pending; the researched scope is the acceptance contract; 6.1 voice held, 6A mobile, connected-service coordination, evaluation-before-fixes and hosting/VM deferrals preserved.

Outcome/scope: owner demonstrates on the selected bot's existing computer, reviews steps and images, generates an editable skill, tests an exact candidate and explicitly publishes/enables; action timeline + keyframes, no continuous video; no host-desktop, microphone or other-bot capture; deliverable is a self-contained native SKILL.md (no executable bundles, macro replay, training, autonomous updates); recording does not sandbox the demonstrated app.

Current-implementation inventory (what exists and the integration consequence): backend/computer.py, docker/runtime_api.py computer routes, pinned native rfb_filter.py and thumbnail.py, web/src/Computer.tsx, backend/knowledge.py, runtime skill routes, plugin/capabilities/service middleware, completed-work skill draft, artifact storage.

Research references table (ShowUI-Aloha, Chrome Recorder, Playwright, Selenium, OpenAdapt, rrweb, WebRobot, Agent Skills, 2026 skill-reusability preprint) with the application to Hermbot; references are not selected dependencies.

Six broader software patterns: event log with visual observations, build-and-promotion pipeline (SLSA, deployment protection), durable jobs/outbox, stable operation identity/idempotency (never replay a GUI action after uncertainty), fencing/explicit ownership, dispatch is not proof of outcome.

Eight-step user flow: Teach a workflow in Computer, take over and wait for input readiness, explicit start with indicator, demonstrate with acknowledged privacy pause, finish and review/parameterize, generate draft from exactly the reviewed evidence, hand back and test on fresh inputs, publish and optionally enable; recording list reachable from Computer and Skills; distinct from Save a completed workflow.

Recording states and invariants: separate ownership/capture/processing/publication fields; lifecycle preparing->recording<->paused->finalizing->ready plus interrupted/discarded/failed; one session per bot; per-event session/generation/segment/sequence/monotonic time/kind/geometry; expected revisions + idempotency keys; finish seals only the persisted prefix; viewer loss pauses capture and keeps human ownership.

Capture at the authoritative boundary: Hermbot-owned observer around the admitted RFB stream, native RfbClientFilter unchanged, fragmentation/coalescing/QEMU keys/clipboard handled, coalesced semantic steps, bounded full-screen keyframes with geometry provenance, no DOM/ARIA claim from the outer page.

Protected input and private evidence: acknowledged private-input pause serialized with observation/frames, privacy generation fences late frames, generic omitted marker only, ordinary Pause for arbitrary screens, no profiles/cookies/headers captured, owner-private (not in Library), reviewed evidence revisions fence processing, screen text is untrusted; redaction is defense in depth.

Storage/retention/limits: PostgreSQL metadata + encrypted private object-store payloads, bounded volatile buffers, staged upload verified before manifest commit, no transaction across upload/model call; proposed 2 frames/s, 2 MiB/frame, 256 MiB/session, one generation job at a time; 7-day expiry with Keep/Delete, discard deletes through a retryable job.

Draft generation: bounded processing job with the existing provider credential, no execution tools, vision support must be verified, normalized events then reviewed segments, persisted hashes/prompt-schema/provider identity/job generation, bounded repair, budget caps; required draft fields and lean SKILL.md rules (name <=64 chars, no credentials/IDs/fixed coordinates).

Testing an unpublished candidate: immutable draft revision bound to bot/config, evidence hash, skill bytes, parameters, checks and authority; task-scoped candidate through the existing supported tool-execution middleware (skill_view), no patching Hermes, no overwriting live skills; ordinary tasks/receipts/budgets/Stop; fresh-input and assertion requirements; candidate consultation is separate evidence from native installation.

Publication/enablement/rollback: current owner authority + exact draft/evidence/test binding, knowledge.guard + native CAS + knowledge_versions + queued refresh, teaching provenance link, pending refresh is not ready, enable only for that bot, rollback as a new draft/version.

Records and API contracts: four record families (session, evidence manifest/chunks, draft revisions/jobs, tests) plus existing records; proposed route family under /api/v1/bots/{bot_id}/teaching; adapter commands carry generation and epoch; no paths/keys from the browser; no screenshots/typed text in SSE.

UI states and accessibility: Teach in Computer, recordings/drafts linked from Skills, no new top-level navigation, status text not colour-only, pane close pauses but keeps human control, reload/logout/restart reconcile and never auto-resume.
Recovery matrix (15 failure rows) and seven implementation slices 6.2.0-6.2.6 (feasibility first); do not wait for 6.3/6.4; voice held, typed annotations; mobile teaching separate.

Acceptance matrix (16 areas) and the real demonstration set (browser form-to-record, desktop/file workflow, collaborative procedure; owner correction, interruption/reconnect, publication conflict/rollback; blocked rather than mocked), plus closing/cleanup rules.

Decisions and remaining validation: proposed choices are not guarantees of universal GUI learning or secret detection; feasibility slice must settle observer implementation, middleware contract, IME/clipboard cases, image limits, vision provider, encryption and retention defaults; UI automation cannot substitute for real owner teaching.

discrepancies.text: Plan says every retained event carries a segment (and that a resolution change opens a new geometry segment); the review repeats that segment accompanies retained observations. The collector increments self.segment on a geometry change but never writes it into events (append adds only seq, generation and time; observe adds geometry), so segment boundaries are not persisted.

Plan section 10 requires persisting prompt/schema version and provider/model identity and processing 'bounded reviewed segments' while keeping completed draft segments after a failure. Code stores provider id/revision/model name/evidence hash in job_provider only, no prompt or schema version, and makes a single chat-completions request (max_tokens 6500, one bounded JSON repair); a failure keeps no partial draft.

Plan section 11/17 describes tests bound to parameters, declared output checks and 'selected current authority', with assertion results from actual files/records; code binds only config_hash/evidence_hash/draft_hash and the checks text. Fresh inputs live only in the task prompt, the optional grant_id is passed to create_task but is not part of the binding, and the pass/fail is an owner-typed boolean plus free-text observations (review row 13 says exactly this), not machine assertions.

Plan section 5/12 requires handing the computer back before agent execution of the test; the backend /test route does not check the human lease (only the UI disables the button while the owner holds control, and publication's knowledge.guard checks human control later).

Plan lists a recoverable 'failed' capture state; the code never sets sessions.state='failed' (failure is the error column or job_state='failed'), 'failed' appears only in the expiry sweep list, and the UI has no label for it.

Plan proposes four record families; migration 018 creates five tables (teaching_publications is the link to knowledge_versions). Plan describes the evidence chunks as encrypted object references, which holds, but reviewed evidence (including selected base64 frames) is also stored encrypted in Postgres (teaching_sessions.evidence_encrypted and teaching_revisions) - up to 6 MiB per frozen revision.

Plan section 10 asks generation to use 'authenticated outbound patterns' with the existing provider credential; the generator calls httpx directly with redirects disabled and 30 s timeouts, not the public-address pinned socket used by backend/connector_http.request (P4-01). Provider URLs may be local, so this may be deliberate, but the plan does not say so.

Plan retention/limit proposals are implemented as proposed (2 frames/s via 0.5 s frame spacing, 2 MiB frames, 256 MiB per session plus 8 MiB volatile buffer, one generation job at a time, 7-day default expiry with Keep) - verified, no divergence; the volatile 8 MiB cap and 6 MiB model-input cap are additions not in the plan.

Plan and review say recordings are not Library artifacts and live in an authenticated teaching namespace; code reuses the artifact bucket (ArtifactStore.bucket) under the 'teaching/' key prefix, so isolation from library objects is by prefix and by never creating artifact rows, not by a separate bucket.

Review claims pane-close requests a privacy pause; the pause is an effect cleanup in Computer.tsx that posts teaching-private-input whenever the Computer panel closes or the bot changes, even when no private input happened, and the backend implements it as the 'private' control action, which also appends an 'omitted: private step' marker each time.

The plan files describe a future/proposal state in their bodies ('Proposed', 'Add a Hermbot-owned observer', 'The feasibility slice must settle', 'Use ... 6.2.0 Feasibility') while the status header (line 3), the review, CHECKLIST:242 and CONTEXT:371 say the milestone is built; the 6.2.0 feasibility gates are not separately evidenced beyond the review's disposable checks.

decisions.decision: Record an action timeline plus selected screen keyframes; no continuous video.
decisions.why: Continuous video is not required to teach or inspect a procedure; keyframes with capture-time/geometry provenance are cheaper and reviewable.
decisions.alternatives: Continuous video/transcoding; a local heavyweight vision stack.
decisions.tradeoffs: Frames after an input are later observations, not completion proof; text legibility depends on the chosen size and was measured only on an idle screen.

decisions.decision: Deliverable is one self-contained native SKILL.md (bounded Markdown).
decisions.why: Preserves the full demonstration-to-reviewed-skill workflow without a second execution platform; ordinary Hermes loop executes it later.
decisions.alternatives: Multi-file executable bundles, general macro replay, model training, autonomous skill updates.
decisions.tradeoffs: Reference material must be summarized into the document; fixed screen coordinates and credentials are excluded.

decisions.decision: Observe accepted RFB bytes in a Hermbot-owned adapter-side observer while the native RfbClientFilter stays the only input gate.
decisions.why: WebSocket packets are not actions and the filter exposes allowed bytes, not a semantic callback; keep authorization unchanged.
decisions.alternatives: Patch rfb_filter, count packets, inject a browser/DOM recorder into the outer page (cannot see a VNC framebuffer).
decisions.tradeoffs: Unknown formats pause capture instead of being guessed; observer parses only the known accepted protocol.

decisions.decision: Protected input needs a server-acknowledged privacy pause serialized with input observation and frame capture, fenced by a privacy generation.
decisions.why: Secure input is ordinary VNC key traffic, so the recorder cannot recognize it; a frontend indicator is insufficient; late screenshots must not repopulate evidence.
decisions.alternatives: Password-field auto-detection in pixels; frontend-only indicator; OCR redaction as primary defense.
decisions.tradeoffs: Capture stays paused until the owner explicitly resumes on a safe screen; redaction/OCR is only defense in depth and secrets elsewhere on screen are not detected.

decisions.decision: Keep recordings owner-private, application-encrypted and outside Library/artifact sharing; metadata in PostgreSQL, payload chunks in the existing object store.
decisions.why: Raw captures are sensitive; reuse existing storage/crypto conventions without adding a public bucket or host port.
decisions.alternatives: Ordinary shared artifacts; a new object store; plaintext workspace fallback.
decisions.tradeoffs: Seven-day default expiry with explicit Keep; deleting does not erase data already sent to a provider or kept by another app.

decisions.decision: Bounded volatile capture buffers; pause (not drop or plaintext-fallback) when private persistence lags; staged chunks verified before manifest commit.
decisions.why: A database failure must not advertise missing chunks and arbitrary actions must not be silently dropped.
decisions.alternatives: Unbounded memory buffering; writing captures to bot workspaces.
decisions.tradeoffs: Capture can pause under load; starting limits (2 frames/s, 2 MiB/frame, 256 MiB/session) are pilot values pending real busy-screen measurement.

decisions.decision: Generate drafts with a bounded application job using the bot's configured provider, no execution tools, and a vision capability check.
decisions.why: Data-to-draft transformation needs no authority; an OpenAI-compatible text endpoint does not prove image support.
decisions.alternatives: Local vision stack; letting the agent execute the generation; unbounded provider loops.
decisions.tradeoffs: One job at a time locally; image support is verified by a generated colour-band canary tolerating one naming error (5/6), which proves processing, not accuracy.

decisions.decision: Freeze exactly the owner-reviewed evidence revision for model processing; edits revoke prior processing and test binding.
decisions.why: Matches the OpenAdapt separation of local captures, reviewed derivatives and approved upload bytes.
decisions.alternatives: Sending raw capture or live editor state to the model.
decisions.tradeoffs: Owner must review frames; images may contain secrets automatic detection misses.

decisions.decision: Test an unpublished candidate through a task-authenticated candidate view delivered by the existing supported skill_view middleware; never install or enable it globally.
decisions.why: A prompt mentioning a disabled skill is insufficient; overwriting a live skill would affect other tasks; Hermes source must stay unmodified.
decisions.alternatives: Temporarily writing the skill natively; patching Hermes; pasting draft instructions and calling it a native test.
decisions.tradeoffs: Candidate consultation is a preview and is not evidence of native installation; a separate post-publish native load/use demonstration is required.

decisions.decision: Bind a test to the immutable draft, evidence and material configuration (runtime/provider/connection) hashes and require a completed, consulted, owner-verified test for publication.
decisions.why: A previously passed test must not authorize changed inputs; build-and-promotion pattern checks the specific artifact before activation.
decisions.alternatives: Badge a version tested on any earlier pass.
decisions.tradeoffs: Owner-observation boolean rather than machine assertions; changed config forces a fresh test.

decisions.decision: Publish through knowledge.guard, native compare-and-swap, knowledge_versions and queued refresh, with a teaching provenance link; rollback is a new draft/version.
decisions.why: Reuse existing publication semantics; a successful write with a pending refresh is not ready.
decisions.tradeoffs: Publish is rejected while work is busy or a human holds the computer.

decisions.decision: Separate state fields, expected revisions and idempotency keys for capture, processing and publication; PostgreSQL jobs without a broker; never replay a demonstrated GUI action after uncertainty.
decisions.why: Fencing and stable operation identity prevent stale tabs/collectors from appending to newer recordings.

decisions.decision: Do not claim browser DOM/ARIA capture from the outer Hermbot page; noVNC/RFB carry framebuffer and low-level events only.
decisions.why: Existing browser tool, Playwright and the desktop do not necessarily share a session.
decisions.tradeoffs: Semantic targets come from owner-reviewed text, not recorded selectors.

decisions.decision: Voice is held; teaching uses typed annotations; mobile teaching is Phase 6A.
decisions.why: Owner put 6.1 on hold and selected 6.2 next.
decisions.tradeoffs: No spoken narration in this milestone.

decisions.decision: Start with a feasibility slice (6.2.0) before dependent slices; real acceptance requires actual owner actions, not simulated API calls or UI automation.
decisions.why: Recorder protocol, middleware contract, vision support and limits are unvalidated assumptions.
decisions.alternatives: Build capture first and validate later; accept scripted demonstrations.
decisions.tradeoffs: Milestone stays unchecked; automated typing into the live desktop was rejected by approval review and never ran.

decisions.decision: Register the specific teaching router before the generic bot lifecycle routes.
decisions.why: Generic /bots/{bot_id}/{action} route consumed the 'teaching' path segment.

decisions.decision: Retry a provider 400 that rejects max_tokens with max_completion_tokens; keep every other provider failure visible.
decisions.why: The initial HTTP 400 was a rejected token-limit parameter, not missing image support.
decisions.alternatives: Treat any 400 as no vision support.
decisions.tradeoffs: Tied to a specific structured error code/param.

decisions.decision: Disconnect pauses only the viewer-bound recording and read-only viewer activity never pauses the owner's recording; pane close requests a privacy pause but keeps human control.
decisions.why: A read-only viewer or stale tab must not disturb the owning session; human ownership persists until explicit handback.

limits.text: Real owner acceptance is not done: owner recording with Pause/Secure input/Resume, exact review/generation, fresh-input/negative/collaborative tests, publication with native refresh and installed-skill use remain pending; the 6.2 milestone box stays unchecked.
Fixture/synthetic evidence only: Chrome rendering used intercepted synthetic records; RFB checks used synthetic packets in disposable containers; none of it counts as owner acceptance.
Approval review rejected automated typing into Scout's live desktop; the script never ran and must not be rerun or indirectly executed.
Capture feasibility was measured on an idle 1440x900 screen (7,981 bytes/frame); busy-screen legibility, CPU/memory and the pilot caps (2 fps, 2 MiB, 256 MiB) remain unmeasured.
Vision check is a six-band colour image tolerating one error (5/6 correct); it proves image processing, not procedure accuracy, so owner review and functional tests remain necessary.
Keystrokes are not proof of final field text (IME, layout, backspace, clipboard); clipboard and geometry-change messages are recorded only as omitted markers; unsupported RFB formats pause capture.

Redaction/OCR cannot prove secret absence; deleting a recording does not erase data already sent to the model provider or retained by another application, and no backup/provider-history erasure is claimed.
A test is a real run (no universal dry-run), and its pass is an owner-attested boolean with observations; candidate consultation is a preview, not native installation evidence.
Single local generation job at a time; a running job is failed after 4 minutes and generation deadline is 120 s with 100 KB response cap.
One example does not establish branches or loops; branch/loop conditions are included only when demonstrated or owner-confirmed.
Not a universal GUI learner or secret detector; Phase 6.2 does not cover voice, mobile-device teaching, VM migration, broad evaluations or connector platforms.
Recording of the owner's real actions does not sandbox the application operated; effects already performed are not undone by discard/delete.

failures.text: Adapter/runtime restart interrupts the recording: the collector's session no longer matches, the row becomes 'interrupted' (retained prefix only) with no input replay.
Object storage or persistence failure: collector heartbeat stops refreshing, pending input is paused after 15 s of lost progress and the owner sees 'Capture persistence unavailable'.

Generation failures (provider changed, vision check failed, invalid skill, deadline/size) set job_state failed with an owner-visible reason; late output is fenced by job token, evidence hash and session state.
Native readback mismatch after publish returns 502 and asks the owner to check native history before retrying.

security.text: Every frame/timeline/revision route is owner-authenticated, requires the session to belong to the bot, and serves frames with Cache-Control: no-store; chunks are application-encrypted and integrity-checked (sha256 + length) on read.
Secret keystrokes never reach durable capture: the barrier pauses the collector first and only an omitted-private-step marker is stored.
Candidate consultation is available only to the task that owns the test (bot identity + active task + sha256 match + config hash + skill_view allowed).

pitfalls.text: C65: generic route precedence - /bots/{bot_id}/{action} swallowed 'teaching'; register the teaching router first.
C65: a prepared recording (capture revision 0) must not be treated as a running collector or become interrupted before Start; allow local discard before any collector exists.
C65: fetch progress is not durable acknowledgement; refresh liveness only on idle health or acknowledged progress and acknowledge only committed prefixes.
C65: asynchronous collection and owner controls complete independently; change state only when collector and control revisions match.
C65: serialize accepted-input observation with the adapter privacy lock, fence asynchronous images by generation and keep capture paused through secret entry.
C65: globally installed skill state cannot serve a task-specific preview; introduce task-authenticated candidate consultation instead of temporary installation.
C65: earlier passed tests must not authorize changed inputs; bind to source, candidate and runtime/provider/connection hashes and require actual consultation.
C65: deleting/expiring a source must stop its executing candidate test through existing cancellation and never switch the task to an installed skill.
C65: a delayed Secure input barrier must not retarget the current desktop ref; keep the original RFB instance and require it still to be current before typing.
C65: load private recordings through a bounded encrypted chunk iterator, not wholly in memory.
C65: accessible names must be explicit for selectors/textareas and callback scope cleared when switching recordings.
Plan pitfall: never let a screenshot taken after an input or a transport receipt stand as proof of application success; test completion needs actual result evidence.
Plan pitfall: do not copy browser profiles, cookies, headers, storage state or raw network bodies into teaching artifacts or skills; Playwright saved state can impersonate.

covered.text: Accepted-RFB fragmentation and clipboard omission; privacy fences against late frames/keys; idempotency and drag boundaries; typing normalization; heartbeat not refreshed on failed persistence.

Start/control/private barrier, encrypted persistence with duplicate poll and review, restarted collector marks interrupted, prepared session waits for owner start, read-only viewer does not pause owner.

Candidate is exact-task-only and config fenced; draft validation and cancel fences generation; vision check with exact input; publish rejects unverified/stale candidates; exact publication versions and stale evidence; source deletion stops active test.
Full backend suite 654 passed (test-results/phase62-backend.xml header), including the 16 teaching tests.

gaps: No real owner recording, native installed-skill use, busy-screen capture measurement or collaborative/negative owner tests yet (review pending list).
Sub-checks like the Computer.tsx pane-close effect and Secure input fence are covered only by build/fixture checks per the review, not by an automated unit test in tests/test_teaching.py.
